frequency_question: How often does institutional friction (inter-agency dissent, public comment friction, legal/procedural delay) prevent a proposed macroprudential capital buffer increase from being finalized above 0% once initiated?
membership_rule: Includes all formal proposals or discussions to raise systemic capital buffers (such as CCyB or SIFI surcharges) by the Federal Reserve Board of Governors. Excludes routine microprudential supervisory rating changes.

cases.name: Basel III Endgame / capital rule major overhaul proposal

provenance_note: claimed 0 hits but 3 of 3 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named major capital framework review cycles; CCyB has historically been maintained at 0% without active friction preventing a raise, rather than a raise being blocked by friction.
known_gaps: The CCyB specifically has never been raised above 0% in US history, making direct base rates for 'raising CCyB' sparse; must use broader macroprudential capital rule adjustments.
skeleton: Regulatory capital adjustment cycles since the post-crisis framework implementation: 3 major regulatory capital setting/review cycles where buffer activation or modification was actively considered by the Board.
multiplier: 3 cycles evaluated, 0 instances where procedural/structural friction completely blocked an intended regulatory adjustment from being formally voted on or advanced, though dilution occurred.
validity_reason: Regulatory governance structures and administrative procedures for the Federal Reserve Board change slowly over decades.
